articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed new plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among the last remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The proposal aims to replace the existing structures with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, on land between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor are all set for demolition. Only the Zedburgh block, which is currently occupied, remains. Andy Roche, a resident of Lower Falinge since 1988, and his partner are the last remaining tenants in the Zedburgh block and have expressed their distress over the plans. Roche stated, "I am not happy about RBH’s proposals, but I’m not sure how to put it into words. My partner is also distraught. We are both autistic and this eviction is making us both really ill."

RBH previously halted demolition plans last year following a successful legal challenge from campaigners. Residents were informed that any future plans would need to demonstrate a clear vision for the land. Despite the new proposals, Roche feels that the concerns of residents have not been adequately addressed. He has been offered alternative housing options by RBH but claims none compare to his current home.

The estate has seen significant changes over the years, with previous phases of redevelopment resulting in 100 new homes since 2012. However, the area has also faced challenges, including being labelled a 'sink estate' by former Prime Minister David Cameron in 2016. The latest plans have reignited concerns among residents about the future of their community.
